data.name: Agem
data.gender_notes: Agem is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Agem is derived from the Sanskrit word 'agni' which means fire. In Hindu mythology, Agni is the god of fire, and this name is believed to signify one who is born from fire or has a fiery spirit. It is a powerful and auspicious name. The name Agem carries the meaning “Born from fire” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Agem usually hope their child will grow to embody born from fire and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name imbued with the power of the divine fire, Agem represents the spiritual flame within.
data.etymology: Agem belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Born from fire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Agem total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference: Agastya Muni is revered as one of the Saptarishis (Seven Sages) in Hindu mythology. He is believed to have lived during the Treta Yuga and is the author of the Agastya Samhita, a major work in Ayurveda.

Agastya is also known as the patron deity of the Agastya Muni Temple located in Tirunallar, Tamil Nadu, India. The temple is believed to have been established during the Chola dynasty, between the 10th and 12th centuries.
